brief_summary: Two-column do/don't map. Left column (amber): axes that are usually safe to mix — matched stem-pole spacing, matched spring free length, similar housing tolerance bands. Right column (caution red): the three mismatches that cause problems — stem poles that don't center causing wobble or binding, springs too long or too short changing reset and force-curve timing, and loose-paired-with-tight housing tolerance stacking into rattle or bind.
data_sources: frankenswitching-explained.mdx § 'Caveats' — 'Stem-pole spacing and wobble. Housings are molded around a specific pole shape and spacing ... Test a single switch through full travel by hand before assuming the fit is clean'

frankenswitching-explained.mdx § 'Caveats' — 'Spring length and weight mismatch. A spring's free length is matched to its housing's compression range at the factory ... a softer or mushier bottom-out than either donor switch had'

frankenswitching-explained.mdx § 'Caveats' — 'Housing tolerance stack-up. Pairing a loose-tolerance bottom housing with a tight-tolerance top (or the reverse) ... Tolerance doesn't blend across a seam; it stacks'
